method: Inductive profiler (JD's skill): conclusions cite their observations, are graded Tentative (1-2 supporting observations) / Probable (3+, none contradicting) / Strong (6+, none contradicting), carry a falsifier, and are scoped to this dataset. Fields of study are taken only where a profile's own data states them (Degrees column, or an explicit degree phrase in the synopsis/footprint); a job alone never counts as a degree. Persona = JD's six rated rows (Big Five + Ego, 1-5); blanks stay blank. Direction uses a +/-0.3 deadband around the directory mean per trait. Lab only — nothing here is filed to any profile.

conclusions.conclusion: Members of the Nursing cohort with Persona ratings sit lower on Openness than the directory average (cohort mean 3.20 vs directory mean 3.60, 5 rated members).
evidence: Allyssa Sabre — Openness rated 3 by JD (directory mean 3.60); field on file: Nursing.
Emma Bortnick — Openness rated 3 by JD (directory mean 3.60); field on file: Nursing.
Katelyn Matthews — Openness rated 3 by JD (directory mean 3.60); field on file: Nursing.
Kourtney Peets — Openness rated 3 by JD (directory mean 3.60); field on file: Nursing.
Contradicting: Hope Kilcollins — Openness rated 4 by JD, on the opposite side of the directory mean; counted against the grade.
conclusions.falsifier: A person whose on-file field is Nursing with a Openness Persona rating of 3.9 or higher, added to this cohort, would stand as further contradicting evidence; enough such ratings to match the 4 supporting ones would withdraw the conclusion.
conclusions.scope: Covers only JD's Persona ratings of the 5 rated members of the Nursing cohort in this directory (13 people carry the field on file). Single instrument — one rater's inputs — so the trait is situational to this dataset. It does not describe people in this field generally, and says nothing about character, motive, or ability.
